newsitem.title: ITALY: Lawyers' strike hits trial of Algerian in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers' strike hits trial of Algerian in Italy.

text.p: The trial of an Algerian charged with supplying arms to Islamic guerrillas was postponed on Wednesday due to a strike by lawyers against proposed legal reforms, judicial sources said.

They said the trial of Djamel Lounici, who was arrested in Italy in May 1995 on suspicion of links with the armed wing of the Algerian Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), would probably begin in May. No precise date was immediately available.

Lounici is also awaiting extradition to France where he was tried in absentia earlier this year and given a five-year jail term for involvement in guerrilla attacks in Marocco, including one in which two Spaniards died in 1994.

He was detained in Italy after a wave of bomb attacks in France in 1995 in which eight people were killed and 160 injured. Italy has said it will extradite Lounici but only after he has faced trial in a Naples court.
